transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-12-03
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Ellis (Redwood AE), Priya Natarajan (Redwood SE), Marta Alvarez (BlueQuarry Head of Platform), Kenji Sato (CTO), Ravi Menon (Integrations Lead)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Quick partner orientation; initial scoping for channel/reseller integration; data residency and KMS discussed; agreed on pilot for 3 models and follow-up benchmark.

[00:00:05] Jordan Ellis: hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, uh, really excited to chat through how Redwood might fit into BlueQuarry's channel roadmap. Marta, you wanna kick off with a quick intro to team and priorities?
[00:00:18] Marta Alvarez: yeah thanks Jordan, hi all. quick intro — BlueQuarry builds an ML inference layer for enterprise search and semantic retrieval for regulated verticals, so our customers care a lot about data residency and auditability. i'm head of platform, r ravi here runs integrations and kenji is our CTO. we're exploring partners for GPU capacity + a reseller relationship.
[00:00:40] Kenji Sato: hi, yeah hi. main constraints: low p95 latency for multi-turn chat, some customers need on-prem or VPC deployments, and encryption with customer-managed keys. cost is also a focus.
[00:00:53] Jordan Ellis: got it. priya and i will cover both the partner program side and the technical surface area — how we support hosted, dedicated and private modes, and what a pilot might look like.
[00:01:04] Priya Natarajan: hey team, quick note on sequencing: we'll want to verify the model family shapes, sequence lengths, and typical qps; that'll inform whether dedicated pools or private deployments make sense. also we often recommend a small benchmark matrix: 1 short-chat model, 1 long-context RAG/embedding model, and 1 mid-size generation model.
[00:01:25] Ravi Menon: that's useful. what's the typical throughput you see for, say, a 16k context model on a single GPU under Redwood's dedicated offering? numbers ballpark.
[00:01:36] Priya Natarajan: ballpark depends on quantization, batching and kernel selection — with our optimized runtime, you might see 20–80 tokens/sec per GPU for FP16/quantized depending on the architecture. but we should run your exact model on a trial cluster to give a proper number.
[00:01:53] Kenji Sato: and in terms of routing, if we have mixed traffic — live low-latency vs offline batch — can Redwood route differently?
[00:02:03] Jordan Ellis: yes, smart routing is a core piece — you can route by latency SLO, cost tier, or region. we also do automated fallback to compatible variants if capacity is constrained.
[00:02:13] Marta Alvarez: on security — we need SOC 2 type II, SAML SSO, RBAC and KMS integration. does Redwood's private deployment support customer-managed KMS?
[00:02:23] Priya Natarajan: yes — private mode supports KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs. for VPC we expose a private control plane and customers can bring their own keys. i will attach our security checklist after the call.
[00:02:34] Ravi Menon: sometimes transcripts from our current provider scramble proper nouns; curious how you handle logs — are logs tokenized? where do they live?
[00:02:44] Jordan Ellis: logs live in the control plane by default for hosted but can be disabled or forwarded; for private you control storage and retention. we can enable redact-by-default for PII.
[00:02:53] [00:10:12] Jordan Ellis: quick pause — i want to sketch the partner engagement model: we have reseller arrangements where partners can resell hosted capacity, plus dedicated pools that can be white-labeled under certain contracts, and private deployment packages for large customers. commissions, commit tiers etc. we can share the playbook.
[00:10:33] Marta Alvarez: for us, the main ask is a simple integration path — ideally an opinionated SDK and clear contract terms for reselling. also, is there a marketplace listing or self-service onboarding for partners?
[00:10:46] Jordan Ellis: yes to both — there is a partner portal and marketplace listing; initial onboarding is fairly self-serve and we provide an engineer orientation pack.
[00:11:00] Kenji Sato: technical deep dive — in private deployment, do you support bare-metal on-prem with our own GPU racks or is it only cloud VPC?
[00:11:10] Priya Natarajan: we support both. on-prem requires a packaging step and some ops integration but we do an on-prem bundle. we've done air-gapped installs before, but there are more checklist steps (networking, certs, monitoring hooks).
[00:11:24] Ravi Menon: what about the KV cache and prefix cache — will that be sharable across nodes or is it per instance?
[00:11:32] Priya Natarajan: good question — our KV cache is managed by the runtime; in Dedicated it's shared across the GPU pool via an efficient distributed cache, in private you can choose a shared cache configuration or local per-node depending on latency and fault tolerance requirements. sometimes transcription tools write KV cache as KV cash — ha.
[00:11:51] [00:20:05] Jordan Ellis: pricing — high level: hosted is pay-as-you-go (per-token + per-embedding), dedicated is a reserved capacity commitment with monthly charges, private has license + support. for channel deals we offer partner discounts and referral fees. i'll send a concrete sheet.
[00:20:23] Marta Alvarez: do you have any minimums for a partner pilot? our ideal pilot is 3 customers over 2 months.
[00:20:31] Jordan Ellis: no hard minimums for a pilot — for dedicated we typically ask for a small commit to reserve capacity, but hosted pilot is usually easiest.
[00:20:41] Kenji Sato: latency guarantees — do you provide SLOs? p95 targets?
[00:20:49] Priya Natarajan: for Dedicated we can provide SLA-backed latency and uptime targets, and we expose token-level cost/latency breakdowns in the console. hosted has best-effort with transparency in performance profiles.
[00:20:59] Ravi Menon: customers in EU need data residency — do you have EU regions with private control plane?
[00:21:06] Jordan Ellis: yes we have EU regions and can deploy private control plane in-region for customers that need residency.
[00:21:12] [00:30:10] Marta Alvarez: integration surface — API shapes, SDKs — we prefer OpenTelemetry hooks and per-request tracing for troubleshooting. can you integrate?
[00:30:19] Priya Natarajan: absolutely — Redwood Console supports tracing hooks and we can send spans to your observability stack or integrate with OTLP collectors.
[00:30:28] Kenji Sato: do you support function/tool calling and structured outputs? we rely heavily on structured extraction from models.
[00:30:36] Priya Natarajan: yes, function calling and structured outputs are supported; we also have an evals pipeline to test regressions against prompt suites.
[00:30:44] Ravi Menon: what's the fastest way to test our on-prem model variant? we have a custom quantized/packed model.
[00:30:51] Priya Natarajan: send us the model artifacts or a representative docker image and we'll spin up a trial runner. for quantized models we may recommend specific kernel paths and a quant profile.
[00:31:01] Jordan Ellis: want to capture a pilot scope: Priya suggested 3 models (short-chat, long-context RAG, generation). BlueQuarry will provide sample workloads and acceptance criteria. Redwood will run perf and cost benchmarks and propose commit tiers based on results.
[00:31:14] Marta Alvarez: acceptable. timeline — we want a pilot in January if possible.
[00:31:20] Jordan Ellis: Jan pilot is feasible; we'll aim to have the trial cluster and benchmark plan agreed by mid-December.
[00:31:27] [00:41:05] Kenji Sato: on the contract side — data processing addendum, reseller terms, and audit rights — are these standard?
[00:41:12] Jordan Ellis: yes we have standard DPA language, reseller addendum and audit provisions. some enterprise customers have bespoke clauses; we can flag any ask early. i'll circulate the initial contract template.
[00:41:26] Ravi Menon: another question — network egress and cost allocation if we're reselling — how do partners account for usage?
[00:41:34] Jordan Ellis: partner/reseller reporting shows partner-level usage; billing can be configured either white-labeled or partner-billed depending on the agreement. we can provide per-token attribution and invoice reports.
[00:41:48] [00:50:00] Marta Alvarez: security docs — can we get your SOC 2 cert and a security checklist?
[00:50:06] Jordan Ellis: yes, i'll attach SOC 2 and our security questionnaire. Priya will also follow up with the VPC deployment checklist.
[00:50:15] Priya Natarajan: i'll also include the ops runbook for on-prem installs — network ports, cert rotation, and the monitoring hooks.
[00:50:23] Kenji Sato: is there any existing reference partner doing a similar reseller model? we'd like to speak to one.
[00:50:30] Jordan Ellis: we can introduce you to a couple of partners — i will check with partnerships and get approvals before sharing customer contacts.
[00:50:38] [00:58:42] Jordan Ellis: recap: action items — BlueQuarry sends workloads and SLOs; Redwood runs a 3-model perf trial; Jordan sends partner playbook, contract template and SOC2; schedule follow-up benchmark session week of 12/10. any other items?
[00:58:56] Marta Alvarez: no that's great, thanks.
[00:59:01] Kenji Sato: thanks everyone.
[00:59:05] Ravi Menon: thanks, talk soon.

End of transcript.
